paper_sections.title: Individual Differences in Anticipatory Somatosensory Cortex Activity for Shock is Positively Related with Trait Anxiety and Multisensory Integration
2.6. General Region of Interest Analysis and Correlation
3.3. Primary Somatosensory Cortex and Individual Differences Analyses

description.value: The study examined fear-conditioning-related somatosensory activity and its relationship with trait anxiety, multisensory integration, amygdala and auditory-cortex activity, and interregional functional connectivity.

design.value: Twenty healthy participants underwent one-run auditory fear conditioning during fMRI. One tone was paired with mild electric shock on 50% of CS+ trials, while the other tone was never paired with shock; participants performed a tone discrimination task.

description.value: An established measure of individual differences in anxiety, with state anxiety (STAI-S) and trait anxiety (STAI-T) scores.

assessment_type.value: measure of individual differences in anxiety

description.value: Peak SCR amplitude from baseline was measured between 1–8 s after CS tone onset on a trial-by-trial basis and averaged as a function of CS tone.

source_definition.value: The first critical regressor was for non-reinforced CS+ trials and the second was for CS− trials.
Trait anxiety score measured with the Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory.

description.value: Twenty healthy participants (11 female) with mean age of 21.95 (range 18–35) participated in the study.

excluded_count.value: no participants were excluded from the analysis post hoc

inclusion_criteria.value: Standard MRI inclusion criteria; participants had to be safe for participation in the MRI environment.

exclusion_criteria.value: Participants who self-reported having a clinically diagnosed mental illness or who reported being on, or having taken in the past, any pharmacological intervention for a mental illness.

medication_status.value: No participants reported being on, or having taken in the past, any pharmacological intervention for a mental illness.

task_description.value: A total of 30 trials were presented in a random order: 10 CS+ with shock, 10 CS+ without shock and 10 CS− tones. CS+ tones were followed by a shock with a 50% partial reinforcement schedule.

instructions.value: Indicate by button press with the index or middle finger of the right hand whether the tone was low or high pitched immediately after hearing the tone.

stimuli.value: Two tones (500 and 1500 Hz) were adopted as conditioned stimuli. A mild electric shock was delivered to the third and fourth fingers of the left hand as the unconditioned stimulus.

description.value: High-resolution T1-MPRAGE structural images were acquired first.
Functional images were acquired with gradient-echo echo-planar T2*-weighted imaging. Each functional volume consisted of 40 interleaved (no skip) 2.5 mm axial T2*-weighted slices.

instrument.value: MP-150 system (BIOPAC System), connected to a grounded RF filter, and MR-compatible leads and electrodes

description.value: Individual skin conductance responses were acquired with MRI-compatible electrodes placed on the index and middle finger of the left hand. All physiological data were recorded at 1 kHz sampling rates.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: The recording is a physiological conductance measure rather than MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET.

description.value: Standard preprocessing was conducted using FMRIBs Software Library (FSL).

steps.value: The first eight volumes were discarded to allow for signal equilibration.
Spatial smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of full width at half maximum (FWHM) 6 mm.
High-pass temporal filtering with a filter width of 100 s.
Skull stripping of structural images with FSL’s Brain Extraction Tool (BET).
Registering each functional image to both the participant’s high-resolution structural image and the standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) 2 mm brain.
MELODIC ICA2 was applied to remove noise components.

model_settings.value: Non-reinforced CS+ trials and CS− trials were modeled during the CS tone interval; six motion parameters and shock-reinforced trials were modeled as covariates of no interest.

hrf_model.value: same temporal epoch for both non-reinforced CS+ and CS− trials

model_settings.value: The shock epoch on reinforced CS+ trials was modeled for 500 ms.

Unique trial-by-trial regressors were created for CS+ no shock and CS− trials, resulting in 20 independent variables. Global mean signal, motion parameters, and shock trials were included in the design matrix as covariates of no interest. Mean parameter estimates for each trial from the right S1 seed were correlated with signal of all other voxels; correlation magnitudes were converted into z scores using Fisher’s r-to-z transformation.

estimator.value: Fisher’s r-to-z transformation and random-effects analysis

model_settings.value: The analysis evaluated total effect c, indirect path a, indirect path b, direct effect c′, and mediation effect ab; A1 was the initial variable, amygdala reactivity the mediator, and right S1 activity the outcome.

description.value: The tone assigned to the CS+ condition was followed by a 0.5 s electric shock.
Non-reinforced CS+ trials in which the tone was not followed by shock.
The CS− tone was never followed by shock.
